Sacred raccoon foxes can’t be killed without “losing luck,” as if the world stops offering you edge cases.
Forest oaths don’t care about crowns. They care about witnesses and seasons.
Druids don’t call this god “good.” They call him alive.

Common sign of recognition
People who honor Waldrun sometimes offer a small salute called the
rabbit-sign: the first two fingers crooked like a pair of ears, starting
curved inward near the chest and then gestured gently outward.
It is less a prayer than an acknowledgment:
the land sees, and is seen back.
See also

Raccoon Fox (Forest Spirit)
Creation Myth: Sun, Moon, Forest
Magical Tattoo Ink

people/npcs/alarich-von-silberhain.title: Magister Argentum Alarich von Silberhain
people/npcs/alarich-von-silberhain.content:
What players would know

Alarich von Silberhain, of
House von Silberhain, is
Banco Valdieri’s ward‑magister—formally
styled Magister Argentum—responsible for vault bindings, ward maintenance,
and the kind of quiet work that keeps confidence from becoming panic. Bank
staff call him “The Abacus” (never to his face).
He presents as meticulous and coldly professional, the sort of man who treats magic like accounting: every ward a ledger entry, every breach a personal insult.
At a glance

Demeanor: calm, exact, hard to impress.
Habits: asks for names, times, witnesses; repeats your words back at you.
Values (publicly): custody chain, procedure, “audit facts.”
What he hates: improvisation, heroics, and anything that makes a clean ledger
impossible.

Common rumors

He can audit a lie the way other people audit numbers.
He is polite right up until the moment you try to skip a step.

See also

Banco Valdieri

people/npcs/althric-von-eichenwald.title: Lord Althric von Eichenwald
people/npcs/althric-von-eichenwald.content:
What players would know

Lord Althric von Eichenwald is an elven noble of
House von Eichenwald, associated
with imperial administration and “quiet oversight” work—the kind of authority
that arrives without fanfare and leaves you rearranging your life around an
appointment you didn’t request.
He tends to present as reasonable and restrained, which is exactly why people take him seriously.

people/npcs/anselm-von-sonnenfels.title: Hochpriester Anselm von Sonnenfels
people/npcs/anselm-von-sonnenfels.content:
What players would know
Hochpriester Anselm von Sonnenfels, of
House von Sonnenfels, is the
Solar Church’s high priest: a public
symbol of doctrine, continuity, and the promise that the Empire’s rituals still
mean what they used to mean.
He is the face people imagine when they think of official faith: immaculate robes, measured speech, and an authority that feels older than the argument you’re trying to have.

people/npcs/ariette-marot.title: Ariette Marot
people/npcs/ariette-marot.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Ariette Marot is a Marcher-born broker of cloth, accent, and presentation who
has survived long enough in the capital to make provincial style look effortless
and respectable. She can source the right marsh colors, explain why a room is
reacting badly, and tell whether someone is really from the Marches before they
finish their first drink.
Common rumors

Ariette charges more to preserve a provincial touch than to remove one.
She can tell who is really from the Marches by how they hold a cup and where
they go quiet in a song.

people/npcs/arnhold-vaelric.title: Arnhold Vaelric
people/npcs/arnhold-vaelric.content:
What players would know
Arnhold Vaelric, known as the Warden of Thorns, is a half-elf warlord who controls a Fey-adjacent gate route in the wilderness. He extracts tolls from travelers and caravans and is tolerated because removing him would cost more than ignoring him—until it doesn’t.
Common rumors

The toll is never just coin.
People come back missing something they can’t name.

See also

Fey Roads

people/npcs/berengar-von-dornfels.title: Arch-Strategist Berengar von Dornfels
people/npcs/berengar-von-dornfels.content:
What players would know
Arch-Strategist Berengar von Dornfels, of
House von Dornfels, is a
high-ranking imperial strategist whose influence is felt more often than it is
seen. People speak his name the way they speak of winter: as something that
arrives on schedule and makes everyone behave differently.

people/npcs/bob-johnson.title: Bob Johnson
people/npcs/bob-johnson.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Bob Johnson is the pretty half of a road-duo currently playing
The Last Lantern Inn: sharp suit, sharp
smile, and a voice that makes heartbreak sound like a confession made too late.
Town criers and fresh posters around the gate district are billing him and
Boy Willie Brown as the “legendary pair from
Statesboro”, which is either true, mostly
true, or the part of the story that helps sell wine.
Common rumors

Bob once played a midnight crossroads and came back better than he had any
right to be.
One verse in every set feels uncomfortably personal to somebody in the room.

people/npcs/boy-willie-brown.title: Boy Willie Brown
people/npcs/boy-willie-brown.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Boy Willie Brown is the quieter half of the Statesboro duo now playing
The Last Lantern Inn. He handles the
backing strings, low harmonies, a low slide-played
Crossing Board, and the part of the room Bob
would miss while smiling at it.
Most listeners remember Bob first and Willie second, which is exactly how Willie
seems to prefer it.
Common rumors

Willie never jokes about crossroads after dark.
If Bob is the legend, Willie is the reason the legend stays alive.

people/npcs/branka-voss.title: Branka Voss
people/npcs/branka-voss.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Branka Voss is a half-orc squad lead in the
Brazen Pike Company, recognizable by
her battered lamellar coat, spell-scorched bracers, and precise convoy
discipline. She has a practical reputation: no speeches, no heroics, no unpaid
risks.
She is the officer currently commanding the Brazen Pike escort attached to
The Broadbarrel Caravan.
Common rumors

Branka does “night stabilization” jobs for people with more coin than honesty.
If Branka says the road is unsafe, she means for everyone else.
She can leave a killing zone “in seven strides” before anyone draws a bead.

people/npcs/bubbling-oozebit.title: Bubbling Oozebit
people/npcs/bubbling-oozebit.content:
What players would know

Bubbling Oozebit is a wiry alley-rogue in Niederstadt with nervous hands and a grin that appears whenever he’s frightened. He’s the kind of person who laughs at the wrong time because silence feels like doom. he has a persistent nasal drip, which makes him sniff frequently.
Common rumors

He can’t stop talking once he starts.
He’s survived things he doesn’t understand by running early.

people/npcs/cael-kohl.title: Cael Köhl
people/npcs/cael-kohl.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Cael Köhl is a polished undercity fixer with a habit of being in the right room
five minutes before trouble starts. She works the edges of guild business around
cards, couriers, and private introductions in Gesso Bianco circles, and she and
the party’s bard already know each other well enough to skip the usual posture.
In Niederstadt she sometimes uses the name Cale, and can be found at
The Broken Seal after dark when she
wants to be reachable.
Common rumors

If Cael asks for payment in favors instead of coin, the information is real.
She can point you toward Gesso Bianco “chalk work” if your ask stays non-violent.
Cael can identify which “pilgrimage logistics” jobs are real and which are covers.
She never discusses sensitive routes in the same room twice.

people/npcs/caspar-renn.title: Caspar Renn
people/npcs/caspar-renn.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Caspar Renn is an arranger and lecturer with a reputation for taking rough
regional material and making it performable in respectable rooms. He is one of
those capital men who can speak admiringly about frontier art for ten minutes
without ever sounding as if he would trust the people who made it.
Common rumors

If Caspar writes a tune down, it stops frightening the city.
He can hear a song once and tell you which parts civilization will not permit.

people/npcs/doc-benway.title: Doc Benway
people/npcs/doc-benway.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Doc Benway is an undercity patch-doctor: the kind of man called when someone
needs stitching, splints, a lie for the Watch, or a second opinion no temple
would sign. He is competent, unsentimental, and widely believed to have saved
more lives than he has ruined, though no one agrees on the ratio.
Common rumors

Benway tells you the price before he tells you the chances.
If Benway says someone is already dead, he usually means the paperwork has not
caught up yet.

people/npcs/dren-malvo.title: Dren Malvo
people/npcs/dren-malvo.content:
What players would know
Dren Malvo is one of the visibly dangerous Brazen Pike veterans: shield forward,
eyes level, no interest in speaking twice.
Common rumors

Dren is where the conversation ends if people keep walking after being told
not to.

people/npcs/duvalli-wine-merchant.title: Mr. Duvalli
people/npcs/duvalli-wine-merchant.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)


Mr. Duvalli is a wine merchant tied to Vellum & Vine, a city-center shop known for tastings, private bottles, and clients who prefer not to be written down too clearly.
He is spoken of as connected to a vineyard outside the city, and as someone who can arrange fast movement of casks when normal couriers are too visible.
Common rumors

Duvalli’s best vintages are never on the menu; they are “for known names only.”
His courier network is cleaner than most guild routes, but only on paper.

people/npcs/ensio-silbermark.title: Captain Ensio Silbermark
people/npcs/ensio-silbermark.content:
What players would know
Portrait

Captain Ensio Silbermark is a cooperative, professional City Watch officer in Hochsilvar. He is tasked with keeping order while balancing guild demands, magistrate expectations, and the practical realities of an underpaid force. The high profile nature of the crime you’re investigating is that an official arrest or identification of the guilty is placing a lot of pressure on him.
At a glance

Demeanor: steady, procedural, quietly exhausted.
Habits: takes notes; repeats key facts back to you to confirm; asks for names and witnesses.
Wants (in public): an answer he can defend in court and in the street.
What he offers: access, introductions, and a measure of official cover—until politics catches up.

Common rumors

Silbermark is “one of the good ones,” which means he’s surrounded.

See also

Banco Valdieri
City Watch
Guard Central Station
Banco Valdieri Investigation

people/npcs/giovanni-valdieri.title: Giovanni Valdieri
people/npcs/giovanni-valdieri.content:
What players would know

Giovanni Valdieri is the high-profile owner of Banco Valdieri in Hochsilvar, known for championing guild-backed promissory notes and the Banking Guild’s growing role in public life.
Common rumors

The Valdieri family enjoys unusual access at court.
Giovanni cares more about “confidence” than truth.

See also

Banking Guild
Banco Valdieri

people/npcs/greta-brandt.title: Greta Brandt
people/npcs/greta-brandt.content:
What players would know
Greta Brandt owns The Brass Buckler, a City Watch watering hole. She looks like
someone who has heard every story twice and believes half of them. She runs a
clean bar in a dirty city and charges extra for anyone who tries to make that
her problem.
Common rumors

Greta can get a message to a captain faster than a runner can.

people/npcs/henrik-bale.title: Henrik Bale
people/npcs/henrik-bale.content:
What players would know
Henrik Bale looks more like a carpenter having a bad week than a mercenary,
right up until he starts examining hinges, chains, and wagon frames with
professional interest.
Common rumors

Henrik can look at a locked crate and tell you whether it was built to keep
thieves out or buyers honest.

people/npcs/henrik-volmar.title: Henrik Volmar
people/npcs/henrik-volmar.content:
What players would know
Henrik Volmar is a practical bulk-goods merchant who runs
The Broadbarrel Caravan: salt pork
jars, ale kegs, and yellow-grass sacks moved in big, boring volume.
He pays for reliable security and predictable paperwork, not heroics.
He is the caravan master who allowed the party to travel with Broadbarrel under
ordinary passenger cover.
Common rumors

Volmar’s margins are thin and his records are clean.
He hires expensive guards because broken cargo bankrupts faster than taxes.

people/npcs/irena-voss.title: Irena Voss
people/npcs/irena-voss.content:
What players would know
Irena Voss keeps The Last Lantern Inn near one of Hochsilvar’s gates. She treats
travelers like weather: unavoidable, often unpleasant, but manageable if you know
when to close the shutters.
Common rumors

Irena always knows who came in last night and who left at dawn.

people/npcs/jannik-kohler.title: Corporal Jannik Köhler
people/npcs/jannik-kohler.content:
What players would know
Corporal Jannik Köhler is a City Watch corporal with the look of a man who
doesn’t sleep enough and doesn’t complain about it. He drinks at The Brass
Buckler with other Watch and keeps his voice low, like the walls can file a
report.
Common rumors

Köhler is “reliable,” which in the Watch means he’s been disappointed often and didn’t quit.

people/npcs/jessa-crow.title: Jessa Crow
people/npcs/jessa-crow.content:
What players would know
Jessa Crow is the Brazen Pike face most likely to smile first and mean it
least.
Common rumors

If a city has kids, lookouts, or drunks for rent, Jessa can usually find
them.

people/npcs/kord-hessel.title: Kord Hessel
people/npcs/kord-hessel.content:
What players would know
Kord Hessel looks like the point where a disciplined mercenary company keeps
its bad idea in reserve.
Common rumors

Kord is calm until he isn’t, and the delay is the dangerous part.

people/npcs/lio-greven.title: Magister Lio Greven
people/npcs/lio-greven.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Magister Lio Greven is an itinerant arithmancer with a nervous scholar’s hands,
a weather-stained robe, and the anxious habit of correcting counts no one asked
him to make.
He travels with a squat Styglian Enumerator
named Nineteen, which he describes as “a bonded tally-witness” whenever someone
calls it a pet.
Common rumors

Greven can count a spilled sack of beans faster than most people can curse
about it.
Nineteen follows him because Greven owns the contract, not because Greven is
in charge.
Greven has never admitted to being lost. He has only been “temporarily
misindexed.”

people/npcs/lorenzo-di-monteluce.title: Ambasciatore Lorenzo di Monteluce
people/npcs/lorenzo-di-monteluce.content:
What players would know
Ambasciatore Lorenzo di Monteluce is the Southern Union’s ambassador to the Empire: polished, cultured, and publicly deferential to imperial tradition. He smiles the way rich men smile in other people’s houses—warmly, as if nothing could possibly be at stake.

people/npcs/lysa-renn.title: Lysa Renn
people/npcs/lysa-renn.content:
What players would know
Lysa Renn has the look of someone who was not hired for her arms and knows it.
Common rumors

Lysa is not the sort of mage you put in front; she’s the sort you keep in
reserve until the scene starts slipping.

people/npcs/marda-flint.title: Marda Flint
people/npcs/marda-flint.content:
What players would know
Marda Flint is a crossbow hand and quartermaster’s shadow with the expression
of someone already counting what will go missing if strangers get too close.
Common rumors

If something is stolen from a Brazen Pike camp, Marda notices before the camp
owner does.

people/npcs/mordecai-orichalcum.title: Mordecai Orichalcum
people/npcs/mordecai-orichalcum.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Mordecai Orichalcum is a tall trans woman wizard and the proprietor of Glass & Moth, a licensed magical item and ingredient shop in the Banco Valdieri Quarter. Her enormous frizzy black curls are just starting to show gray at the edges, and she wears a thin-strapped black dress like it is armor.
She does business from behind a heavy counter, backed by a tall glass case packed with potions, scroll tubes, and a riot of other small magic items that all come with receipts, warnings, and an optional lecture.
See also

Glass & Moth

At a glance

Demeanor: dry, precise, surprisingly kind if you read the fine print.
Tell: ink-stained fingertips, careful hands, unflinching eye contact.
Shop vibe: curated chaos with hard rules about custody and consequences.

Common rumors

She can tell a cut potion by smell from across the counter.
If you try to steal from her, you forget what you came in for.
She keeps one shelf in her display case empty, like it is waiting for something to come home.

people/npcs/needle-sava.title: Needle Sava
people/npcs/needle-sava.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Needle Sava is a gossip-runner and rumor broker in Niederstadt who appears
wherever people are paying to know things quietly. She works tavern edges and
shrine lanes rather than guild halls, and sells introductions more often than
hard evidence.
Common rumors

Needle never sells one buyer’s name to another buyer.
If she smiles before naming a price, the price is about to hurt.

people/npcs/ollo-krev.title: Ollo Krev
people/npcs/ollo-krev.content:
What players would know
Ollo Krev is the sort of compact mercenary who makes doorways feel smaller.
Common rumors

Ollo is bad news in a stairwell and decent company once the contract is over.

people/npcs/oskar-damm.title: Oskar Damm
people/npcs/oskar-damm.content:
What players would know
Oskar Damm runs The Broken Seal in Niederstadt. He looks like a man who never
gets surprised twice: plain clothes, plain speech, and eyes that do the counting
before the coins hit the table.
Common rumors

Oskar can introduce you to someone who can introduce you to someone.

people/npcs/pietro-sarto.title: Pietro Sarto
people/npcs/pietro-sarto.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Pietro Sarto is a stable boy and runner at the Valdieri family quarters in
Hochsilvar’s Imperial City. He knows tack, schedules, and which doors servants
are allowed to use. He is a young half-elf, around sixteen, with white hair,
blue eyes, and the start of a wispy beard. He is polite to anyone in good cloth
and wary of anyone who asks questions like a magistrate. He is from
Statesboro in
The River Marches, which is why any talk of
Bob Johnson and Boy Willie Brown gets through his professional composure faster
than most things do.
He is one of the party’s servant-side contacts on the Valdieri thread.
Common rumors

He “sees everything” because he is always carrying something from one place to
another.

people/npcs/raffaele-valdieri.title: Raffaele Valdieri
people/npcs/raffaele-valdieri.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Raffaele Valdieri is a minor Valdieri cousin: the kind of family member who gets invited to dinners for appearances and quietly managed the rest of the time. In Hochsilvar’s rumor economy, he’s “the problem relative” with expensive tastes and unreliable judgment.
Common rumors

He’s always one bad decision away from being cut off.
He disappears for weeks, then returns with new clothes and no explanation.

people/npcs/rex-flavus.title: Rex Flavus
people/npcs/rex-flavus.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Rex Flavus is a Ponte Nero routing clerk who works the night shift around
animal-exchange paperwork and delivery sequencing. He has a reputation for
keeping his hands clean while everyone else gets dirty.
He is the paperwork source who pointed the investigation toward
Henrik Volmar and
The Broadbarrel Caravan.
Common rumors

Rex can make a manifest disappear by “correcting” it.
If Rex says a route is late, someone important already moved.

people/npcs/sabine-korber.title: Sabine Korber
people/npcs/sabine-korber.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Sabine Korber is a capital hostess known for elegant small-room evenings where
musicians, minor officials, ambitious young nobles, and carefully selected
provincials are made to seem as if they belong in the same moral weather. She
has a reputation for “discovering” rough talent and presenting it in a way the
city can admire without feeling threatened.
Common rumors

If Sabine praises your “natural force,” she is about to remove whatever made
you dangerous.
An invitation from Sabine can mean opportunity, inspection, or both.

people/npcs/saheera-al-zahret.title: Matriarch Saheera al-Zahret
people/npcs/saheera-al-zahret.content:
What players would know
Saheera al-Zahret is a prominent desert matriarch associated with Traveler politics and caravan-route negotiations. In settled lands she is spoken of as a “caravan queen.” Among route people, she is spoken of as someone who can make an argument about water sound like law.

people/npcs/serak-thorn.title: Serak Thorn
people/npcs/serak-thorn.content:
What players would know
Serak Thorn is Branka Voss’s lieutenant in the
Brazen Pike Company: a hard-faced
contract sergeant who speaks like every word is part of a checklist.
On the Broadbarrel run, he is the one most likely to handle procedure, guard
discipline, and any conversation that sounds like a problem.
Common rumors

If Branka is elsewhere, Serak is the one who keeps the company from turning
into twelve separate problems.
He doesn’t bluff much because he usually doesn’t need to.

people/npcs/tamas-vale.title: Tamas Vale
people/npcs/tamas-vale.content:
What players would know
Tamas Vale is the one Brazen Pike arcanist people underestimate because he
looks more like a tired scholar than a battlefield problem.
Common rumors

Tamas is dangerous only if you forget how much trouble a practical wizard can
cause.

people/npcs/thane-jager.title: Thane Jäger
people/npcs/thane-jager.content:
What players would know
Portrait (player-safe)

Thane Jäger is spoken of as the kind of imperial field operative people name
only after the door is shut. He has a tall reputation for taking the jobs
everyone else calls impossible, ugly, or suicidal, then returning with the
objective somehow complete and half the room too unsettled to ask how.
Common rumors

If Jäger accepted the contract, the job was already worse than anyone said.
Thane outlived too many teams to be lucky alone.

people/npcs/toliver-brune.title: Toliver “Tolly” Brune
people/npcs/toliver-brune.content:
What players would know

Toliver “Tolly” Brune is a street vendor who reliably appears wherever the Royal Games gather crowds. He is aggressively friendly, addresses everyone as “my lord” (duke, stablehand, and street urchin alike), and sells a hot snack that is almost a meal.
His stall sign reads:

TOLLY’S HONEST MEALS
SAUSAGE IN A BUN
(NAMED MEAT)

Tolly insists this is a mark of integrity. When pressed, he produces a small ledger and says, “Transparency, my lord. Every sausage recorded. First names only. Privacy laws.”
At a glance

Demeanor: too cheerful, too close, never embarrassed.
Pitch: calls his product “fully licensed” and waves a stamp that is never quite right.
Tell: he smiles like he has already won the argument, even when he is clearly losing.

Common rumors

If you eat his food before a big bet, your luck turns “honest” (for good or ill).
Nobody has ever caught him lying; he only speaks in legal shapes of truth.

people/npcs/velka-dorr.title: Velka Dorr
people/npcs/velka-dorr.content:
What players would know
Velka Dorr is a Brazen Pike scout and convoy rider who looks impatient even
when standing still.
She was the party’s first point of contact on the Broadbarrel road and reads
the verge like other people read a ledger.
Common rumors

If someone breaks from the road and thinks distance will save them, Velka is
usually the answer.

people/npcs/vile-piglit.title: Vile Piglit
people/npcs/vile-piglit.content:
What players would know

Vile Piglit is a back-alley “rogue” in Niederstadt with an oversized swagger and a weapon he clearly can’t afford to lose. He talks like a veteran and moves like someone who learned intimidation from overheard stories.
Common rumors

He practices threats in a mirror.
He’s “connected,” but only in the way a stray dog is connected to a street.

people/npcs/ysra-venn.title: Ysra Venn
people/npcs/ysra-venn.content:
What players would know
Ysra Venn is the kind of caravan guard people notice only after realizing
someone has already checked the roof, the lock, and the alley behind them.
Common rumors

If Ysra was seen clearly, she either wanted that or didn’t mind it.

people/pcs/Ben/frenunulemulo-sheet.title: Frenunulemulo Character Sheet
people/pcs/Ben/frenunulemulo-sheet.content:
What players would know
Frenunulemulo is a half-elf warlock with a sharp social edge, a deep mistrust of
divine beings, and an explicit connection to The Silent Poet.

Class / level: Warlock 3
Species / background: Half-Elf / Custom Background
Core feel from the sheet: persuasive, observant, and built for social pressure
more than physical confrontation

people/pcs/Niki/ishtar-sheet.title: Ishtar Character Sheet
people/pcs/Niki/ishtar-sheet.content:
What players would know

Ishtar is a wood-elf rogue and former acolyte: quiet, observant, persuasive,
and built for infiltration rather than open confrontation.
She joined the party at the handler briefing before the Broadbarrel pursuit and
has quickly settled into the role of covert road operative.

Class / level: Rogue 3
Species / lineage / background: Elf / Wood Elf / Acolyte
Core feel from the sheet: observant infiltrator built for stealth, sleight of
hand, persuasion, and careful positioning

people/pcs/Roo/gashesh-netz-gloom-stalke.title: Gashesh Netz Character Sheet (Gashesh.pdf)
people/pcs/Roo/gashesh-netz-gloom-stalke.content:
What players would know
This version of Gashesh Netz is a half-orc ranger with strong martial presence,
shadow-oriented ranger training, and a practical caravan-and-guard history.

Class / level: Ranger 3
Species / background: Half-Orc / City Guard
Core feel from the sheet: tall, dangerous, quiet, and built for ambush work

people/pcs/Roo/gashesh-netz-sheet.title: Gashesh Netz Character Sheet
people/pcs/Roo/gashesh-netz-sheet.content:
What players would know
Gashesh Netz is a human ranger with soldier training, heavy physical capability,
and a deliberate, controlled demeanor.

Class / level: Ranger 1
Species / background: Human / Soldier
Core feel from the sheet: strong, accurate, and disciplined rather than flashy

people/pcs/Thandi/aurelia-sheet.title: Aurelia Character Sheet
people/pcs/Thandi/aurelia-sheet.content:
What players would know
Aurelia is a half-elf bard built for talk, reading a room, and bending outcomes
through charm, performance, and Lore-college interruption.

Class / level: Bard 3
Species / background: Half-Elf / Custom Background
Core feel from the sheet: high social competence with a strong investigative side

people/pcs/Warren/bianca-montelupo-sheet.title: Bianca Montelupo Character Sheet
people/pcs/Warren/bianca-montelupo-sheet.content:
What players would know
Bianca Montelupo is a moon-circle druid with strong practical magic, serious
survivability, and a sheet that leans toward animal handling, perception, and
field utility.

Class / level: Druid 3
Species / background: Human / Farmer
Core feel from the sheet: durable, high-Wisdom, and built to shift forms under pressure

people/pcs/Warren/bianca-montelupo.title: Bianca Montelupo
people/pcs/Warren/bianca-montelupo.content:
What players would know

Bianca Montelupo is a compact, unsentimental druid with a raven familiar and a
procedural attitude toward “nature magic”: boundaries, cycles, and the price of
interference.
She currently operates under imperial paperwork (Joint Task Force / continuity
authority), with the practical implication that she goes where she’s told and
asks the questions she’s permitted to ask.
Common rumors

She doesn’t talk about her home grove.
She trusts procedures more than promises.

quests/q-banco-valdieri-investigation.title: Banco Valdieri Investigation
quests/q-banco-valdieri-investigation.content:
What the party knows (briefing version)
A high-profile robbery has struck Banco Valdieri in Hochsilvar, threatening public confidence in the new promissory-note system.
It happens midway through the capital’s solstice week festival, The Royal Games: the city is crowded, tempers are short, and everyone with a warrant or a knife is using the noise as cover.
The City Watch has sealed the scene under a three-day magical quarantine, and the Banking Guild is demanding results loudly enough that even honest clerks can hear it.
You are assigned to a Joint Task Force: City Watch investigators and the Crown-authorized domestic intelligence arm operating across the feudal states.

Known facts

The vault shows signs of unusual arcane interference.
The bank is under Guard quarantine while forensic wizards examine the scene.
The Royal Games crowd turns every street into an argument, and every empty bed into a commodity.
The breach occurred at noon on the solstice—an auspicious hour in Solar Church calendars.

Objective (as given)
Identify who stole the refined magic, determine where it is headed, and recover it if possible.
See also

Refined Magic
The Royal Games

What the party can reasonably discover
If you push on the right doors (and survive the politics), you can uncover:

Bank-scene receipts: time distortion evidence; missing-time inconsistencies; a “rain underground” signature locals won’t stop talking about.
Paper trails: promissory-note signet chains; custody-chain anomalies; documents that look too clean to be honest.
Undercity leads: smuggling logistics; territorial tells; a name that never comes with a face.
Transport constraints: refined magic moves like fragile contraband, which creates slow routes, choke points, and opportunities for interception.

races/beast-adjacent-symbiotes.title: Beast-Adjacent Symbiotes
races/beast-adjacent-symbiotes.content:
What players would know
In some regions, semi-domesticated predators live alongside communities in uneasy partnership. They blur the line between livestock and ally: night sentries that don’t sleep as deeply as people do, hunting partners that understand territory better than any sheriff.
The relationship is practical. Food, shelter, and ritual handling in exchange for protection and teeth. It works—until it doesn’t.
Common rumors

Longhouse chiefs sleep better when a symbiote curls under the roof.
Some symbiotes understand commands better than militia recruits.

races/dwarves.title: Dwarves
races/dwarves.content:
What players would know
There are no dwarves on this world. Playable ancestries are limited to elf, half‑elf, human, and half-orc.

races/elves.title: Elves
races/elves.content:
What players would know
Elves are long-lived custodians of harmony and stability: stewards of archives, forests, and heraldry—people who think in decades and act as if patience is a moral virtue. Their counsel props up noble legitimacy, their paperwork outlasts wars, and their aesthetic sense makes even oppression look calm.
They move slowly on decisions, preferring careful curation over quick action. That slowness can feel like wisdom or like indifference, depending on who is bleeding.
Elves commonly live up to ~1500 years. That long horizon shapes everything: debts, favors, grudges, and “temporary” measures that become policy.
Common rumors

Elvish bloodwardens quietly veto marriages.
Elves hoard the oldest maps and songs.

races/fey.title: Fey
races/fey.content:
What players would know
The Fey are dangerous, transactional beings whose courts migrate and whose presence warps time along the Fey Roads. They bargain the way merchants bargain—precisely, relentlessly—except the goods are often memories, names, years, and the shape of a promise.
People who survive an encounter often describe it the same way: as if the memory itself can’t decide what happened, only that it mattered.
Common rumors

Fey deals pay out in madness.
Time slips worst near Fey gates during moon-change.

races/humans-living-in-the-elven-empire.title: Humans
races/humans-living-in-the-elven-empire.content:
What players would know
Most of the Empire’s population is human or half‑elf. Outside the high nobility, citizenship and daily life are more local than imperial: towns and villages run on bargains, grudges, and practical alliances, rarely unified for long.
Imperial authority is thin, so local lords, guilds, mayors, and caravans negotiate power deal by deal. “The law” is often whoever arrived last with a seal and enough people to enforce it.
Common rumors

Every province is controlled by one of the elven noble houses and has its own petty war brewing usually with neighboring provinces over some imagined slight or old grudge or contested resources, access to trade routes and so on the way petty neighbours usually feud.
Paper notes and guild favors matter more than crowns.

races/humans-living-in-the-human-majorit.title: Humans
races/humans-living-in-the-human-majorit.content:
What players would know
In the human-majority countries, most towns and villages are human-run but rarely unified. Alliances form around trade, marriage, and shared threats, then dissolve when the next season’s problems arrive.
Imperial authority (where it exists at all) is thin. Local lords, guilds, and caravans negotiate power deal by deal, and a hard winter can redraw “politics” faster than any decree.
Common rumors

Every province has its own petty war brewing.
Paper notes and guild favors matter more than crowns.

races/ifrit.title: Ifrit
races/ifrit.content:
What players would know
“Ifrit” is the common name for fire-willed beings associated with volcanic country and hot, thin places where stone remembers heat. People argue about whether they are spirits, elementals, demons, or something older than those categories. The argument doesn’t matter much at the edge of an ash valley.
Most folk who claim to have seen an Ifrit are describing the consequences: scorched footprints that don’t match any boot, voices carried by heat shimmer, and the feeling that the air itself is deciding whether you are permitted to breathe.
Common rumors

They keep contracts better than nobles.
They punish clever wording by taking it literally.

races/orcs.title: Orcs
races/orcs.content:
What players would know
Orcs are fully woven into society as caravan guards, dock muscle, negotiators, and fixers. In trade hubs and border towns, they often serve as go‑betweens—people who can speak to guild enforcers and honest merchants in the same hour without flinching.
They’re common enough to be unremarkable and networked enough to be dangerous to underestimate.
Many orc families also come from hard country—high passes, faultland corridors, and the edges where roads become suggestions. Those orcs tend to be practical about wilderness: you don’t “conquer” terrain; you negotiate with it.
In politics, orcs are often the Empire’s most reliable bridge to the places where imperial law becomes a rumor: they understand contracts, witnesses, and long memory, and they take “trust” seriously because it is a resource that can be spent.
Common rumors

Every trade hub has an orc crew that can move anything.
Orc bosses keep books better than nobles.
If you need to cross a mountain pass without dying of weather, you hire an orc guide… and you don’t argue about their rules.
Some imperial agents travel with openly seconded orc liaisons—because the Empire is learning it can’t buy certain kinds of access with coin alone.
